decision.title: Arithmetic and comparison operators (packet )
decision.summary: Arithmetic and comparison operators have their own enums, take atomized operands, use int64 fast paths with libmpdec beyond, and follow the listed rules for durations, dates and value, general and node comparisons.

body.p: . src/operator_internal.h; src/operator.c (operands, promotion, numbers, unary), src/operator_temporal.c (durations, dates, times), src/operator_compare.c (value, general and GNode comparisons).

item.p: Interface: own enums (sxml_arithmetic_operator, sxml_comparison_operator, sxml_node_comparison_operator), not the IR's, so the function library and later front ends share them; operands are atomized sequences (atomizing is the evaluator's), results owned; the implicit timezone and, for untyped-to-QName casts, namespace bindings travel in the request. Non-atomic items are INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Numbers: int64 fast paths with checked arithmetic, else libmpdec; integer div gives xs:decimal; xs:float computed in double and rounded once; idiv and mod of doubles are exact (int64 within 2^53, else exact decimals; no libm). Decimal LIMIT_EXCEEDED (digit or heap byte limit) is FOAR0002.

Durations (PR2628): any xs:duration times/div a number cast to xs:decimal (shortest digits, ); months by fn:round#1, nanoseconds half to even; NaN FOCA0005, times INF or div 0 FODT0002, div INF zero. Dates: 400-year cycle days (Hinnant), so every int64 year works; results beyond it FODT0001, differences beyond int64 seconds FODT0002.

Comparisons: value = NaN rule + fn:compare (sxml_atomic_item_compare with the heap's name pool, ); general: untyped vs number cast to the number's primitive type, else xs:double; vs string or untyped compared as text; else cast to the other primitive type; left outer, first error ends. GNode: document order (equal only for the same node).

Known problem (fixed by ): libmpdec's large-number multiplication (six_step_fnt/transpose_pow2, stack buffers of up to 128 KiB) overflowed the 64 KiB WebAssembly stack: 10^6000 * 10^6000 trapped under wasm. moves the buffers to the heap; the operator tests may now multiply at the digit limit.
